items.headline: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
items.blurb: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
items.text: A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said. Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment. The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said. Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days. Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said. "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said. The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons.

items.text: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. items.text: US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, and a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties". The Ukrainian leader's comments came after US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory. items.text: Hamas has confirmed that Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in an Israeli air strike on the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza. Israel’s military and Shin Bet security agency earlier said in a joint statement that they had targeted a senior Hamas military commander in a drone strike in Khan Younis on Saturday. The attack that hit a tent sheltering displaced people wounded two others. The casualties were taken to Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, medical personnel told Al Jazeera on Saturday. Video footage verified by Al Jazeera and posted by Palestinian journalists from the vicinity of the hospital showed ambulances inside the grounds and stretchers that appear to be stained with blood. Al-Mawasi, a coastal strip on the Mediterranean, is crowded with displaced Palestinians living in tents. Israel has repeatedly attacked the area despite previously designating it a humanitarian zone. items.headline: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
items.blurb: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.
items.text: Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670m; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent. Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app. It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately. The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts. Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery. items.headline: Hundreds of men march in Switzerland to protest violence against women
items.blurb: Organisers say men must speak out, as Swiss study finds half of men aged 18 to 24 hold restrictive view of masculinity.
items.text: Hundreds of men have led a demonstration in Switzerland’s capital, Bern, to denounce misogyny and violence against women, saying men need to take a more effective role in fighting both. The “Men Against Violence Against Women” rally outside parliament on Saturday follows persistent concerns that misogyny is too prevalent online among teenage boys and young men and that other men need to build a stronger counter-narrative. The misogynistic views are pushed by the right-wing “manosphere” – a loose network of online forums and influencers that promote male supremacy and hostility to feminism. Such influencers were emboldened after Donald Trump won the US presidential election in 202 to justify and amplify misogynistic derision and threats online. “We men are part of the problem – the problem being violence against women and queer people,” said Christoph Gosteli, a 42-year-old social worker who co-organised the rally with a group called maenner. “That is why it is important for us to take a stand and say, ‘We no longer want to be part of the problem; we want to be part of the solution.’”

items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.headline: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
items.blurb: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".
items.text: SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time. "Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas. The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower. But the first catch of the rocket's booster was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday. The booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames just above the sea. The top part, known as the Ship, returned to Earth a few minutes behind schedule at around 15:20 local time (21:20 GMT) on Saturday, in the first-ever successful catch attempt.

items.headline: Noel Tata on Tata Trusts’ twin roles: Philanthropy, projects of national importance
items.blurb: Plans include building lasting institutions, developing a network of 40 to 50 nonprofit hospitals and pursuing partnerships with other philanthropies.
items.text: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has introduced a two-part plan for the country’s oldest and largest charity group: continue giving, but measure it by the results, and keep supporting Tata Sons ’ investments in important national projects. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, the 70-year-old Tata Trusts chairman said the charitable institutions would have two distinct but complementary roles. “One part is the direct philanthropy, which we do. So building institutions, giving grants to other NGOs, or alleviating hardships directly with beneficiaries. The second is through Tata Sons, to invest and nurture projects of national importance,” said Noel. “We are, from a trust perspective, we stand 100% behind Tata Sons’ efforts to build these projects and invest in projects of national importance,” he said, noting that this is part of the institution. “And while continuing the philanthropy work, and basically we end up with a balance between some direct philanthropy, which happens every year, and some money going towards investment in national projects.” Noel said these investments were not necessarily detached from commercial considerations.

items.blurb: He was subsequently taken into custody by the Keralam police in connection with a case registered in the Thrissur district.
items.text: A 20-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of sensitive locations in Mumbai, including the Chabad House, a Jewish community centre, on the instructions of international criminal syndicates and anti-national elements, an official said on Saturday. Yash Singh, a resident of Airoli in Navi Mumbai, was initially detained by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) based on inputs regarding his social media contacts with anti-national handlers. He was subsequently taken into custody by the Keralam police in connection with a case registered in the Thrissur district in the southern state, the official said. Singh told the police that he was tasked by social media handlers linked to mafia gangs and subversive elements to carry out recce of sensitive areas of South Mumbai, particularly around Colaba. "His assignments included photographing and pinpointing the exact locations of the Chabad House, businesses owned by Jewish individuals, and areas frequented by foreign nationals. items.headline: Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises
items.blurb: Drought has devastated Maharashtra’s Beed district, pushing women farmers and labourers towards distress migration. Despite repeated pleas for employment, villagers say government job guarantees have failed them, even as the State announces a ₹6,728-crore package
items.text: Women of Takarwan village in Beed have been fighting for work under Employment Guarantee Schemes for the last two years. This year, they say, they will fight for work under VB-G RAM G, as they do not want to migrate to feed their families. | Photo Credit: Vinaya Deshpande Pandit The cotton plants are green, but the bolls are missing. Across the Chauhan family’s four-acre field in Majalgaon in Maharashtra’s Beed district, the plants stand stunted, their promise of a harvest withered by the absence of rain. What should have been a season of cotton picking has become a search for the few bolls the drought has spared. Under the relentless October sun, Vanita Chauhan bends over the plants, picking the little cotton she can find. A tattered towel covers her head, shielding her from the scorching heat. Her full-sleeved shirt is buttoned up to her neck, while the red pallu of her sari is tied around her arm and neck, fashioned into an improvised pouch. She drops each cotton boll into it before moving hurriedly to the next plant.

items.text: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday said the state government would tighten traffic enforcement following an accident in Golaghat district that killed 26 people on Friday. Sarma visited the accident site on Saturday afternoon and ordered a detailed investigation. “A detailed investigation is underway, and we will look at every possible cause behind this tragedy,” he said. He said the state government had earlier relaxed traffic rules, which, according to him, was not the right decision. “I admit that some traffic decisions were relaxed at the Nalbari Cabinet meeting because of political pressure. Even then, I felt we should not have given in, and it will not happen again. We will bring back strict traffic rules and enforce them firmly, because people’s lives come first,” he wrote on X after the visit. Sarma also announced that the state government would provide compensation of ₹ 7 lakh to the families of the deceased. items.text: Aayush Wellness enters shilajit supplement market with Himalayan drops (Image - Company website) Aayush Wellness Ltd has entered the shilajit-based wellness supplement segment with the launch of Himalayan Shilajit Drops, seeking to diversify its nutraceutical portfolio and tap growing demand for products targeting energy, stamina and vitality. The launch comes amid projected growth in the global shilajit market, which was valued at $206.64 million in 2025 and is expected to reach $436.72 million by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 8.67 per cent during 2026–34, the company said in a statement. Asia-Pacific accounted for around 61 per cent of the global market in 2025, while liquid shilajit products made up 60.72 per cent, indicating the growing relevance of the region and liquid formulations, it said. Aayush Wellness said its new product contains Himalayan-sourced shilajit extract in liquid-drop form and is positioned to support daily energy, stamina and vitality. The formulation is described as rich in fulvic acid and minerals, with heavy-metal testing. items.headline: ‘Holy Grail of spaceflight’: SpaceX pulls off first-ever midair 'catch' of Starship returning from orbit
items.blurb: SpaceX achieved the first catch of a Starship spacecraft, guiding the 171-foot vehicle into the arms of its launch tower after a 22-hour orbital mission. The ship completed 14 laps around Earth and deployed 26 Starlink satellites, while its booster exploded shortly after liftoff.
items.text: Elon Musk-owned SpaceX on Saturday (local time) pulled off the first-ever ‘catch’ of a spaceship, marking a milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems. SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, crucial for rapid and low-cost recycling. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. According to Reuters, the 171-foot-tall Starship fell out of thick clouds over SpaceX's Starbase launch site, reignited engines to flip itself vertical, and slowly descended into the tower's "Mechazilla" arms, engines still roaring. Charred from the blazing heat of its return from space, the ship shut down its engines and hung still after the rocket system's longest mission yet. The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 124-meter behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the US-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. items.blurb: Beauty calendars have become a Christmas staple and have become particularly popular with female shoppers.
items.text: It's easy to see the appeal of a beauty advent calendar. Like many women at this time of year, Julia says she often finds herself tempted to splurge on one - especially a perfume calendar. But she takes quite an unsentimental approach. "I always look at what's in them. If I like enough of the fragrances, I'll buy it," says the 39-year old, who works as a senior commercial manager in engineering. Luxury advent calendars are supposed to offer the thrill of a surprise but, for Julia, it is more important she actually wants the items inside - a thought that is also striking more and more customers in the wake of the scandal over the Skims calendar. This week, Kim Kardashian's beauty brand offered all of its customers refunds for its $148 (£110) calendar after being widely criticised on social media over the quality of its contents, with some customers likening the hair clips, scrunchies and keychains inside to things you might find down the back of a sofa. items.blurb: JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Allison Beer, who runs a credit card business ranking among the world’s largest, is departing to work somewhere else.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Allison Beer, who runs a credit card business ranking among the world’s largest, is departing to work somewhere else. Beer “has informed me of her decision to leave the firm for an external opportunity,” Co-President Troy Rohrbaugh told staff Friday in a memo, a copy of which was obtained by Bloomberg. The largest US lender will appoint a successor for the card and connected commerce business in the coming weeks, he said. Beer, a veteran of American Express Co., joined JPMorgan in 2017 and has expanded its credit-card franchise, sometimes with offerings that competed fiercely with her former employer by targeting travelers and other heavy spenders. Early this year, JPMorgan reached an agreement to replace Goldman Sachs Group Inc. as the partner for Apple Inc.’s credit card. So no-one gave Wales a glimmer of hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30–1 during the week. The question, not of when but can Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953. That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. The outpouring of unbridled emotion after a losing run - stretching across 34 matches - that has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.” In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “AI takeover.” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military.” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. items.headline: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.blurb: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
items.text: Last month, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. More recently, privacy-focused AI assistant Ollie announced its shutdown a few weeks ago. Aside from Character.ai and Ollie, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry. Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .”

Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. items.headline: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. items.text: On The Vergecast: The many spiraling stories in the AI world, the fate of streaming services, Mark Zuckerberg’s meat, and more. On The Vergecast: The many spiraling stories in the AI world, the fate of streaming services, Mark Zuckerberg’s meat, and more. One part of the saga surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ended on Thursday, when Huang resigned from his position at the top of AI’s most important company. But in the coming weeks and months, a much bigger story may be about to unfold. A story about Nvidia’s dealings in China, about the US government’s willingness to turn a lot of blind eyes to protect a powerful ally, and about the very stability of the AI industry as a whole. It’s a lot. On this episode of The Vergecast , David and Nilay start by trying to unpack the many parts of the story. items.headline: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.blurb: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
items.text: The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims. The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service. While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang. U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. items.headline: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.blurb: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
items.text: Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday. That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence. With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. items.headline: Jensen Huang’s Exit: How Deep Does NVIDIA’s AI Ecosystem Run In India?
items.blurb: Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA has put the spotlight on the company’s leadership and succession plans. But for India, the…
items.text: NVIDIA’s influence in India extends far beyond GPU sales, spanning AI infrastructure, software, developer ecosystems, startup incubation and direct equity investments. With Indian data centre operators committing billions of dollars to NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, and enterprises and startups building on its CUDA-led software stack, the company has become deeply embedded in the country's AI ambitions. As Jensen Huang exits, the bigger question is whether India can reduce its dependence on a single technology provider, particularly as geopolitical uncertainties, export restrictions and competing chip architectures reshape access to AI compute. Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA has put the spotlight on the company’s leadership and succession plans. But for India, the more consequential question is what happens to an ecosystem that has increasingly come to depend on the American chipmaker for its AI ambitions. From data centre operators ordering thousands of GPUs to startups building on its software stack, NVIDIA has established relationships across almost every layer of India’s AI industry.
